name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) takes place in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July and targets PhD students and young researchers working in all aspects of AI. The programme offers introductory and advanced courses, specialised tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and a rich social programme including a reception at the Vienna City Hall. Participants can attend parallel tracks, network with international peers and world‑renowned speakers, and benefit from the city’s historic academic environment.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and the University of Oslo and takes place at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, and focuses on multilingual large language models, their evaluation, data curation, and dialectal challenges. The program combines technical talks, hands‑on sessions, and field activities such as a ski‑friendly location and bus transfers, and participation is subsidized by the OpenEuroLLM project with no registration fee.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI summer school taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. The program aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine learning and artificial intelligence topics. It welcomes enthusiasts, students, academics, and industry professionals to learn and collaborate.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of computer‑vision topics, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed for students and early‑career researchers seeking advanced training in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The MLx Health & Bio programme is part of the Oxford Machine Learning School’s 2026 offerings. It runs from 10 to 13 July 2026 in a hybrid format, focusing on applying the latest representation learning and generative AI advances to healthcare and biomedical challenges. Topics include AI in imaging, computational biology, real‑world health data, multi‑omics, drug discovery, and population health epidemiology.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden. It brings together doctoral and postdoctoral researchers to discuss topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making through keynotes, industry talks, brainstorming sessions and student presentations. The program is hosted at the Happy Tammsvik resort and includes indoor and outdoor ice‑breaker activities, with all accommodation and meals sponsored for participants.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI for robotics, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience on state‑of‑the‑art systems. The programme targets master’s‑level students and industry practitioners, providing networking opportunities and a special summer school dinner.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, and forensic science. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers and professionals, offering intensive lectures by leading experts, hands‑on sessions, and the possibility of scholarships and a limited‑capacity, in‑person experience.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems is held at Umeå University in Sweden. It offers lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session and a social program to explore ethical, legal and societal challenges of AI and AS. The three‑day event (11–13 March 2026) targets researchers, students and professionals and provides networking opportunities alongside practical exercises.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM’27) will be held in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble, France, from 1‑5 February 2027. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking on topics such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction. The mountain setting provides opportunities for outdoor activities and fosters cross‑disciplinary collaboration among academia and industry participants.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The Winter School runs from 11 – 15 January 2027 as part of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference. It focuses on deep‑learning research, covering state‑of‑the‑art methods in image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The event gathers national and international researchers in Tromsø to foster collaborations and share cutting‑edge advances.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
venue: Kathmandu World School, Suryabinayanak, Kathmandu, Nepal
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an 11‑day in‑person program held at Kathmandu World School in Kathmandu, Nepal from 28 December 2026 to 7 January 2027. It offers intensive AI lectures, hands‑on labs and project work covering fundamentals and advanced topics such as geometric deep learning, world models, generative modeling and neuro‑symbolic AI, aimed at senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty and industry professionals. The school seeks to bring together international experts to share cutting‑edge research, build AI skills in the region and foster collaborations among participants.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School took place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. The program featured lectures and tutorials by leading researchers from institutions such as Google DeepMind, MIT, and the University of Cambridge, covering a broad range of machine‑learning topics. Although the application deadline has passed, the school provided participants with hands‑on sessions, networking opportunities, and exposure to cutting‑edge AI research.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School offers a focused five‑day program of keynotes, lectures, and practical sessions led by experienced AI experts. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, emphasizing topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics in machine learning. The school promotes diversity, networking, and collaboration through scholarships, optional poster sessions, and cultural or social activities.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI takes place at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers five days of expert lectures, hands‑on labs, and project work aimed at master, Ph.D., post‑doc and early‑career researchers interested in state‑of‑the‑art AI techniques. Participants will also benefit from networking events and mentorship opportunities designed to build the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing (AthNLP) Summer School 2026 is held at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. The program, organized by a consortium of research centres and universities, offers intensive lectures and hands‑on sessions on state‑of‑the‑art NLP methods for students and researchers. It runs from 2 to 8 September 2026 and is followed by the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Chania.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning. It offers theoretical foundations and hands‑on experience with topics such as clustering, GANs, self‑supervised learning, anomaly detection, and unsupervised reinforcement learning, targeting STEM students with intermediate AI knowledge. The residential (or online) format runs from 29 June to 17 July 2026 and equips participants with career‑relevant skills and a solid basis for future research.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars in Caen, Normandy, France. It focuses on applying deep‑learning techniques to accelerate scientific research, covering topics such as machine learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations. The programme combines lectures with hands‑on Python workshops using libraries like NumPy and PyTorch to give participants practical experience in implementing AI models for scientific problems.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive programme offering courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, inventive thinking and the intersection of business and technology. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students who can attend a combination of online learning and an on‑campus teaching week at the Lappeenranta campus, while also enjoying a social programme in Finnish nature. The school emphasizes hands‑on workshops, group work and networking opportunities within a multicultural environment.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the inaugural International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, held in Porto–Maia, Portugal. The four‑day event (30 March–2 April 2026) offers parallel courses, a symposium, and open‑debate sessions for graduate students, post‑doctoral researchers and industry practitioners interested in AI’s foundations, risks and societal impact. Participants can attend face‑to‑face or join live online, with all lectures recorded and available for 45 days after the school, and they receive a certificate of participation.
